probe_review.assessment: Encoded scalar used in host length arithmetic under fixed consumer semantics; runtime effect conditional.
Matching host decode; only local representation is normal.
Representation is decoded but complete length is not certified; missing header cannot be inferred from names.
Widening count does not decode stored endian representation.
Decoder width does not match direct scalar declaration.
Visible override defeats fixed helper semantics.
synthetic-v1 source and synthetic-other declaration have no same-revision provenance.
Candidate assignment does not uniquely establish later consumed value.
Conditional initialization is outside the bounded straight-line value-flow contract.
Visible consumer override prevents certification of byte-count semantics.
Direct encoded-byte copy has no eligible integer length assignment; it is not whole-function normal.
Bounded object/source identity is not certified after rebinding; rejection is not proof that rebinding is faulty.

limitations: Static expectations were reviewed; no detector outcome is certified by this audit.
Known-source development does not establish blind or independent detection performance.
Decode-without-header normal means only local representation, never complete byte length.
Header version reuse is metadata-based provenance derivation, not actual include binding or a fresh fixed-revision export.
API/helper names and source ordering do not establish linked kernel implementations, CFG first execution or full function dataflow.
Zero and symmetric values can hide effects; actual values, configuration, reachability and preprocessing remain unknown.
